structured_output.hypothesis: If Darwin is right, then among mammal species coded as terrestrial (non-volant, non-marine) and native on islands more than 300 miles (~483 km) from a continent or great continental island, essentially none exist.
structured_output.pass_criterion: After excluding bats, marine mammals, domesticates and human-introduced populations (using the PHYLACINE present-natural range, which removes human-caused range changes), the number of non-volant terrestrial mammal species whose present-natural range includes an island lying more than 483 km from the nearest continent or continental island of at least 100,000 km2 is 0 to 2, and each of those is on inspection a documented introduction or an island misclassified as oceanic.
structured_output.fail_criterion: Three or more non-volant terrestrial mammal species have a present-natural range on islands more than 483 km from a continent or large continental island, and each is confirmed from the literature as native (not human-introduced).
structured_output.interpretation: Darwin's "terrestrial mammal" means non-volant, non-marine mammals; he explicitly treated bats as able to cross the sea. His "300 miles" is converted to 483 km. "Continent or great continental island" is operationalized as a shelf-connected landmass of at least 100,000 km2. "Native" is operationalized with the PHYLACINE present-natural range, which is the range without human impact and includes Late Quaternary extinct species. Modern reinterpretation: Holocene-extinct endemics (for example, island rodents) count as native counterexamples, which Darwin could not have known. "Free from doubt" is mapped to a manual literature check of every candidate. The method overlays the PHYLACINE range rasters (about 96.5 km cells) with a global landmass layer such as Natural Earth and uses the trait table's terrestrial/marine/aerial flags. Limitation to report: coarse cells resolve small islands poorly.

dataset.name: Data from: PHYLACINE 1.2: The Phylogenetic Atlas of Mammal Macroecology
dataset.why_it_fits: It gives present-natural and current range rasters for all extant and recently extinct mammals, plus a trait table with terrestrial/marine/aerial flags, order and family. Overlaying present-natural ranges with island geometry lets us count native non-volant terrestrial mammals on remote islands.
